brief.headline: Update Claude Code now — bash permission bypass patched, try /teleport
brief.summary:
Claude Code 2.1.223 closes a real hole: a crafted bash command could previously hide parts of itself from permission checks, so update before your next unattended run. The same release ships /teleport, which pulls a finished cloud session down to your machine — worth wiring into the describe-it-and-sleep loop you're already running. Pair it with codeseek, a Rust MCP tool that gives an agent call-graph and hybrid semantic search over your repo, so it stops guessing at structure and asking you where things live during a long overnight session.

On cost, a cluster of new control-plane repos (opencodex, claudexor, omnigent, and a Codex-backend adapter for Claude Code's dynamic workflows) all do the same thing: let you keep Claude Code or Codex as your interface while routing execution to Ollama, DeepSeek, Gemini or whatever's cheapest per subagent. dao-code sweetens this specifically for DeepSeek-V4 by engineering byte-stable prompt prefixes so cross-session memory barely adds token cost — a real lever for your longest-running sessions. And on the oversight side, a 40,000-run study found humans miss about one in three genuinely dangerous agent commands when eyeballing approval prompts — treat that as confirmation that your permission hooks and allowlists need to catch what you won't, and look at fable-method's 'prove' skill as a scripted verification step before a diff ever reaches your review queue.
bullets: Update to Claude Code 2.1.223 and run claude --teleport to pull a finished cloud session onto your machine

Clone opencodex or claudexor to point subagents at Ollama, DeepSeek or Gemini backends and cut per-turn spend; claudexor adds quota-aware rotation across subscriptions plus cross-model review of the final diff
Try tigicion/dao-code as a DeepSeek-V4 backend for your longest sessions — its cache-reusing prompt prefixes keep cross-session memory nearly free
Install CodeBendKit/codeseek as an MCP tool so agents navigate call graphs and semantic search themselves instead of asking mid-run
Bolt fable-method's 'prove' skill onto your prompt as a self-verification pass before an agent opens a PR
Don't trust manual approval prompts as your safety net — humans missed 1 in 3 dangerous commands across 40k runs, so lock down permission hooks/allowlists instead

items.title: DenisSergeevitch/agents-best-practices — Provider-neutral Agent Skill for Codex, Claude Code, and agentic harness design.
items.tldr: agents-best-practices packages a provider-neutral Agent Skill for harness and prompt design, usable directly in Codex or Claude Code.
items.whyItMatters: A ready-made skill file for agentic-harness design you can drop into your skills folder tonight instead of writing one from scratch.
items.tryThis: Clone DenisSergeevitch/agents-best-practices and copy the skill into your Claude Code skills directory.

items.title: CodeBendKit/codeseek — Rust-powered code intelligence CLI for AI coding agents. Builds call graphs and hybrid semantic search indexes (Dense + Sparse + RRF + Reranker) across 7 languages. Ships as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex
items.tldr: codeseek is a Rust CLI that builds call graphs and hybrid semantic search indexes (dense + sparse + RRF + reranker) across 7 languages, exposed as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex CLI.
items.whyItMatters: Better code retrieval lets an unattended agent navigate and verify a large codebase itself instead of guessing or asking you where things are — a direct lever for longer unsupervised runs.
items.tryThis: Clone CodeBendKit/codeseek, build the index for your repo, and register it as an MCP tool in your Claude Code config.

items.tldr: Claude Code 2.1.223 fixes a Bash permission-bypass exploit, adds owner-wildcard entries for marketplace allow/block lists, and ships a /teleport hint for resuming cloud sessions locally.
items.whyItMatters: The permission-bypass fix is a real security patch — a crafted command could previously hide parts of itself from permission checks — and /teleport is a direct route from an overnight cloud run to a local morning review.
items.tryThis: Update Claude Code to 2.1.223 and run claude --teleport to pull a finished cloud session onto your machine.

items.title: omnigent-ai/omnigent — Omnigent is an open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness: orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents — swap harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in rea
items.tldr: Omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and custom agents interchangeably, with policy enforcement, sandboxing, and control from any device.
items.whyItMatters: A single control plane to swap harnesses per task and to check on or steer agents from your phone instead of being tied to your desk.
items.tryThis: Clone omnigent-ai/omnigent and route one subagent through it to test cross-device control and its sandbox policies.

items.title: lidge-jun/opencodex — Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code — use any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama…) with Codex CLI, App, SDK, and Claude Code
items.tldr: opencodex is a proxy that lets Codex CLI/SDK and Claude Code call any LLM backend — Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, or local Ollama models.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you route cheap or bulk agent work to a local/open-weight model while keeping your existing Claude Code or Codex workflow, cutting spend without switching harnesses.
items.tryThis: Clone lidge-jun/opencodex and point one subagent's model config at a local Ollama model to test cost savings tonight.

items.title: Waishnav/devspace — Turn ChatGPT into Codex! OR Turn Claude Web into Claude Code!
items.tldr: devspace turns the ChatGPT web app into a Codex-like coding agent, or Claude's web chat into Claude Code, from the browser.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you kick off or steer a coding agent from a phone or tablet browser session without a terminal, useful for controlling agents away from your desk.
items.tryThis: Clone Waishnav/devspace and try driving a small task from Claude Web on your phone.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method distills the workflow behind 'Claude Fable 5' into reusable skills plus a think/act/prove eval loop meant to keep any model's output honest.
items.whyItMatters: The 'prove' step is a concrete self-verification pattern you can bolt onto your own agent prompts to get closer to a genuinely reviewable PR instead of trusting the agent's say-so.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method and adapt its 'prove' skill as a verification step before your agent opens a PR.

items.title: tigicion/dao-code — Open-source TypeScript terminal coding agent for DeepSeek-V4 — builds on DeepSeek's strong price-performance and ultra-cheap cache pricing, engineering byte-stable prefixes and cache-reusing forks so cross-session memory
items.tldr: dao-code is an open-source terminal coding agent tuned for DeepSeek-V4, engineering byte-stable prompt prefixes so cross-session memory and self-correction add almost no extra token cost, and it's config-compatible with Claude Code.
items.whyItMatters: DeepSeek-V4's cheap cache pricing plus this repo's prefix engineering is a concrete way to cut per-turn token spend on long unattended sessions without abandoning your Claude Code setup.
items.tryThis: Clone tigicion/dao-code and swap it in as a cheaper backend for your longest-running, highest-turn agent sessions.

items.title: Javis603/token-monitor — Local-first desktop widget for tracking token usage, costs, and limits across 28+ AI coding tools—including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and OpenClaw—with multi-device sync.
items.tldr: token-monitor is a local-first desktop widget tracking token usage, cost and rate limits across 28+ coding tools including Claude Code and Codex, synced across devices.
items.whyItMatters: One real-time cost readout across every harness instead of checking separate dashboards — useful once you're routing work across multiple models and subscriptions.
items.tryThis: Install Javis603/token-monitor and point it at your Claude Code and Codex usage to see actual per-tool spend tonight.

items.title: withkynam/vibecode-pro-max-kit — Your AI forgets. This remembers. Spec-driven coding harness for vibecoders, product owners, CEOs and real builders — self-improving context memory, 15 agents, 33 skills working with /goal, agent-team, & work
items.tldr: vibecode-pro-max-kit is a spec-driven Claude Code/Codex harness with /goal and agent-team commands that runs multi-agent workflows on autopilot with zero human approval gate.
items.whyItMatters: It's a direct, ready-made template for the 'describe the work, go to sleep' loop you're building toward — worth trialing before rolling your own.
items.tryThis: Clone withkynam/vibecode-pro-max-kit and run /goal on a small feature to see whether its no-human-gate autopilot loop actually holds up.

items.title: razzant/claudexor — Multi-harness control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode: quota-aware rotation across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions, shared thread context, and cross-model review.
items.tldr: claudexor is a control plane that rotates work across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions by quota, shares thread context across harnesses, and runs cross-model review.
items.whyItMatters: Quota-aware rotation avoids rate-limit stalls on long unattended runs, and cross-model review gives an agent's finished PR a cheap second opinion before you wake up.
items.tryThis: Clone razzant/claudexor and route your overnight run through it to add automatic cross-model review of the final diff.

items.title: scasella/claude-dynamic-workflows-codex — Run Claude Code dynamic workflows on a local Codex (GPT) backend, plus an interactive run viewer
items.tldr: This repo runs Claude Code's dynamic workflows on a local Codex (GPT) backend, with an interactive viewer for watching the run.
items.whyItMatters: Keeps Claude Code's workflow orchestration while routing execution to a cheaper/local backend, and the viewer helps you verify what happened without re-reading raw logs.
items.tryThis: Clone scasella/claude-dynamic-workflows-codex and rerun one existing dynamic workflow against the local Codex backend to compare cost and output.

items.title: Humans missed 1 in 3 threats approving AI agent commands across 40k game runs
items.tldr: Across 40,000 game runs, humans approving AI agent commands missed roughly one in three that were actually dangerous.
items.whyItMatters: If you're relying on manual 'approve this command' prompts as your safety net for overnight runs, this says that net has a real hole — automated policy checks matter more than your own vigilance.
items.tryThis: Audit your permission hooks/allowlists so genuinely dangerous commands are blocked by policy, not caught by you eyeballing a prompt at 2am.

clusters.title: Wave of multi-harness, cost-routing control planes
clusters.summary: Four new repos independently solve the same problem: keep Claude Code or Codex as the interface but route actual execution to whichever model or subscription is cheapest, with rotation and cross-model review layered on top.

clusters.title: The verification gap between agent output and human trust
clusters.summary: One item ships a scripted 'prove' step to make agent output self-checking; the other shows why that matters — manual human approval of agent commands misses a third of real threats.
